questions.stem: The host-derived envelope is removed from an otherwise intact influenza virion. Which function should decline most sharply?
options: Receptor-mediated entry
Capsomere assembly
Viral RNA synthesis
Copying of host DNA
questions.explanation: Influenza envelope glycoproteins attach to host receptors and mediate membrane entry. Removing the envelope damages this earliest host-recognition step.

questions.stem: Why can the genome of a positive-sense RNA virus begin directing protein synthesis soon after uncoating?
options: It contains host ribosomes
It acts directly as mRNA
It first becomes a prion
It is always double-stranded
questions.explanation: Positive-sense RNA has the same readable orientation as mRNA, so host ribosomes can translate it directly.

questions.stem: A negative-sense RNA virus enters a cell without a functional RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. What is the most immediate consequence?
options: Its capsid cannot attach
Its DNA cannot integrate
Its genome cannot produce readable mRNA
Its envelope becomes bacterial
questions.explanation: Negative-sense RNA is complementary to mRNA. A viral polymerase must first make a positive-sense RNA that host ribosomes can read.

questions.stem: Which description identifies a provirus rather than a free virion?
options: Protein-only infectious agent
Circular plant RNA without capsid
Complete particle outside a host cell
Viral DNA integrated into host DNA
questions.explanation: A provirus is a viral DNA stage integrated into the host genome. A virion is the complete extracellular infectious particle.

questions.stem: A viral genome becomes enclosed by a complete capsid. Which outcome follows most directly?
options: The nucleic acid becomes better protected outside the host cell
The virus fails to infect that cell efficiently
It cannot independently synthesize proteins or reproduce
The phage attaches to a susceptible bacterium
questions.explanation: The nucleic acid becomes better protected outside the host cell. Capsid proteins shield the genome from nucleases and environmental damage.

questions.stem: Which change most directly explains this observation: the nucleic acid becomes better protected outside the host cell?
options: A virus lacks a surface protein able to bind a cell's receptor

questions.explanation: Burst size is progeny released per infected cell: 16,000 ÷ 200 = 80. It is not the total number of particles in the culture.

questions.explanation: Comparable intracellular genome numbers indicate entry occurred. Reduced viral protein production points most directly to translation, although later replication can also fall as a consequence.
